units.title: Reported speech
units.intro: Reported speech shifts tense and pronouns when the reporting verb is past.

cards.title: Backshift basics
rule: Direct: *“I am ready,” she said.* → Reported: *She said (that) she was ready.*
will → would; can → could; have done → had done.
*tell* needs a person object: *He told me to wait.*

examples.text: She said she is tired yesterday.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "She said she is tired yesterday."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** Direct: *“I am ready,” she said.* → Reported: *She said (that) she was ready.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "She said she is tired yesterday." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "She said she was tired."
**Check:** will → would; can → could; have done → had done.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: He said, ”I had seen the film before.”

options.A: He said that he has seen the film by now.
options.B: He said that he has seen the film before.
options.C: He said that he had seen the film before.
options.D: He ordered that to see the film.

cards.why: When the direct speech is already in the Past Perfect ('had seen'), it remains in the Past Perfect in indirect speech. Note: Option B uses 'has seen' (Present Perfect), which is incorrect. Option C is the correct conversion.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: He said that he had to go at once.

options.A: The boy said, ”I will have to go at once.”
options.B: The boy said, ”I must to go at once.”
options.C: The boy said, ”I have to go at once.”
options.D: The boy said, ”I had to go at once.”
options.E: The boy said, ”I want to go at once.”

cards.why: When converting indirect speech with 'had to' back to direct speech, 'had to' usually changes back to 'have to' or 'must'. Option B is grammatically incorrect ('must to' is wrong). Therefore, 'I have to go at once' is the correct direct form.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: They said that they were going to church. (Change to Direct Speech)

options.A: They said, “They were going to church.”
options.B: They said, “We were going to church.”
options.C: They said, “We are going to church.”
options.D: They said, “They are going to church

cards.why: To change from indirect to direct speech: the past continuous 'were going' changes back to present continuous 'are going', and the pronoun 'they' (referring to the speakers) changes to 'we'.

cards.title: Questions and commands
rule: Wh-questions: keep the wh-word; use statement order.

examples.text: She asked if I was ready.

examples.fix: She asked if I was ready.

examples.text: He told us to sit down.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "She asked was I ready."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** Yes/No: *asked if/whether* + clause (no do-support).
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "She asked was I ready." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "She asked if I was ready."
**Check:** Wh-questions: keep the wh-word; use statement order.

cards.answer: She asked if I was ready.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: Backshift: present→past, past→past perfect, will→would; keep place/time words consistent.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Use told + person, said (that)…; adjust tense when the reporting verb is past.

cards.title: Quick check

options.A: She said that where were you.
options.B: She asked me where I was.
options.C: She said to me that where have I had.
options.D: She asked me where was I.
options.E: She asked me where I had been.

cards.why: The Present Perfect **'have been'** changes to Past Perfect **'had been'**. In indirect questions, the subject ('I') comes before the auxiliary verb ('had').

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: She said to them, “Have you ever seen a scorpion?”

options.A: She asked them if she saw a scorpion.
options.B: She asked them whether they have seen a scorpion.
options.C: She asked them whether they had seen a scorpion.
options.D: She asked them whether they has seen a scorpion.
options.E: She asked them if she had seen a scorpion.

cards.why: For Yes/No questions, we use 'if' or 'whether'. The tense changes from Present Perfect ('have seen') to Past Perfect ('had seen'). The pronoun 'you' changes to 'they' to match 'them'.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the correct indirect speech form: **"When are we going to submit the group assignment?" the students said to the teacher.**

options.A: The students asked the teacher if they were going to submit the group assignment?
options.B: The students asked the teacher if they were going to submit the group assignment.
options.C: The students asked the teacher when they were going to submit the group assignment.
options.D: The students asked the teacher whether they are going to submit the group assignment.
options.E: The students asked the teacher whether they are going to submit the group assignment?

cards.why: In reported speech for 'Wh-' questions, the question word ('when') is kept, and the word order changes from question to statement (subject + verb). The tense shifts from Present Continuous ('are going') to Past Continuous ('were going').

glossary.meaning: moving tenses one step back in reported speech

tips.text: Backshift: present→past, past→past perfect, will→would; keep place/time words consistent.

games.title: Match the form to its example

questions.q: The director asked me ________ to the project meeting scheduled for the next morning.
questions.label: 1. The director asked me ________ to the project meeting schedu

similar.q: The director asked me ________ to the project meet
The school principal warned the students ________

options.A: if I will come
options.B: whether I would come
options.C: whether would I come
options.D: if will I come

why: Answer B: whether I would come

This is a reported Yes/No question. It requires the complementizer 'if' or 'whether', followed by declarative word order ($$\text{if/whether} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$). Because the reporting verb 'asked' is past, the future 'will' must backshift to 'would'.
Option C and Option D incorrectly invert the subject and auxiliary. Option A fails to backshift 'will' to 'would'. Only Option B correctly implements both backshifting and declarative word order.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The school principal warned the students ________ inside the laboratory compound.
questions.label: 2. The school principal warned the students ________ inside the

similar.q: The school principal warned the students ________
She told me that she ________ her university appli

options.A: to not run
options.B: not to run
options.C: do not run
options.D: not running

why: This is a reported negative command. Negative commands are reported using the structure: $$\text{reporting verb} + \text{object} + \text{not to} + \text{V}_{\text{base}}$$.

Students often place the negative particle 'not' after 'to' (Option A), resulting in 'to not run', which is a common split-infinitive error. Option B is correct because 'not' must strictly precede 'to'.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: She told me that she ________ her university application the day before.
questions.label: 3. She told me that she ________ her university application the

similar.q: She told me that she ________ her university appli
The police officer asked the driver where ________

options.A: submitted
options.B: has submitted
options.C: had submitted
options.D: was submitting

why: The time-marker 'the day before' indicates that the original speech contained the Simple Past ('yesterday'). In reported speech with a past reporting verb, Simple Past must backshift to Past Perfect ($$\text{Simple Past} \rightarrow \text{Past Perfect}$$).

Students often choose Simple Past 'submitted' (Option A), failing to apply the backshifting rule. Present perfect 'has submitted' (Option B) is incorrect because it cannot represent a completed past action in reported speech.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The police officer asked the driver where ________ his car during the morning rush hour.
questions.label: 4. The police officer asked the driver where ________ his car d

similar.q: The police officer asked the driver where ________
The biology teacher stated that plants ________ su

options.A: had he parked
options.B: he had parked
options.C: did he park
options.D: he has parked

why: This is a reported Wh-question. It must follow declarative word order ($$\text{Wh-word} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$). Because the original question was in the past tense ('Where did you park?'), the verb must backshift to Past Perfect.
Option A and Option C incorrectly maintain interrogative inversion. Option B 'he had parked' correctly uses declarative word order and the backshifted Past Perfect tense.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The biology teacher stated that plants ________ sunlight to manufacture their food.
questions.label: 5. The biology teacher stated that plants ________ sunlight to

similar.q: The biology teacher stated that plants ________ su
Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the nati

options.A: needed
options.B: need
options.C: had needed
options.D: are needing

why: The reported statement describes a scientific fact (general truth). General truths are an exception to the backshifting rule and remain in the Simple Present tense ($$\text{S} + \text{V}_{\text{1/s/es}}$$).
Students blindly apply backshifting to 'needed' (Option A) because they see the past reporting verb 'stated'. This is a common conceptual trap on national exams.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the national examination next month.
questions.label: 6. Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the national exami

similar.q: Dawit says that he ________ ready to take the nati
The director asked me ________ to the project meet

options.A: is
options.B: was
options.C: will be
options.D: has been

why: The reporting verb 'says' is in the Present Simple. When the reporting verb is in the present, no backshifting is applied to the reported clause.
Students often automatically backshift to 'was' (Option B) because they assume all reported speech is past. Option A 'is' is correct because the reporting verb is present.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.label: 7. She asked me why ________ her the previous night as we had a

similar.q: The director asked me ________ to the project meet

options.A: didn't I call
options.B: I hadn't called
options.C: I didn't call
options.D: hadn't I called

why: This is a reported negative Wh-question. It must follow declarative word order ($$\text{Why} + \text{Subject} + \text{Verb}$$). Because 'the previous night' indicates a past action, the verb must backshift to Past Perfect.
Option A and Option D incorrectly maintain subject-auxiliary inversion. Option B 'I hadn't called' correctly uses declarative word order and the backshifted Past Perfect tense.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The administrative assistant ________ that the registration office was temporarily closed.
questions.label: 8. The administrative assistant ________ that the registration

similar.q: The school principal warned the students ________

options.A: told
options.B: said me
options.C: said
options.D: told to me

why: The reporting verb is followed directly by a *that*-clause. The verb 'said' does not require a personal object, whereas 'told' must be followed by a personal object ($$\text{Subject} + \text{said} + \text{that-clause}$$).

Option A and Option D are incorrect because 'told' requires a personal object ('told me'). Option B is incorrect because 'say' cannot be followed directly by a personal object without 'to'. Option C is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: He wanted to know how many candidates ________ for the regional examination.
questions.label: 9. He wanted to know how many candidates ________ for the regio

similar.q: She told me that she ________ her university appli

options.A: had registered
options.B: did register
options.C: have registered
options.D: were registering

why: This is a reported Wh-question. The original question 'How many candidates have registered/registered?' must backshift to the Past Perfect ($$\text{S} + \text{had} + \text{V}_3$$) because the reporting verb 'wanted to know' is past.
Students often choose 'did register' (Option B) or 'have registered' (Option C), failing to apply backshifting. Option A is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The suspect admitted that he ________ the national archive building the night before.
questions.label: 10. The suspect admitted that he ________ the national archive b

similar.q: The police officer asked the driver where ________

options.A: entered
options.B: has entered
options.C: had entered
options.D: enters

why: The time-marker 'the night before' indicates that the original speech contained the Simple Past. In reported speech with a past reporting verb, Simple Past must backshift to Past Perfect.
Students often choose Simple Past 'entered' (Option A), failing to apply the backshifting rule. Past Perfect 'had entered' (Option C) is correct.
questions.tip: Read the whole sentence, find the clue word, then test each option.

questions.q: The teacher said to the student, “Will you revise your lessons at home?”

options.A: The teacher asked the student if she would be revised her lessons at home.
options.B: The teacher asked the student if she will revise our lessons at home.
options.C: The teacher asked the student if would she revise our lessons at home.
options.D: The teacher asked the student if she would revise her lessons at home.
options.E: The teacher asked the student if she will revise her lessons at home.

why: In reported questions, 'said to' becomes 'asked'. For yes/no questions, we use 'if' or 'whether'. The future 'will' changes to 'would', and the pronoun 'you' changes to 'she' (or he).
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Choose the correct indirect speech form: **The teacher said to the student, "Do you revise your lessons at home?"**

options.A: The teacher asked the student if she revised her lessons at home.
options.B: The teacher asked the student if she had revised her lessons at home.
options.C: The teacher asked the student if did she revise her lessons at home?
options.D: The teacher asked the student if she revises her lessons at home.
options.E: The teacher asked the student if she has revised her lessons at home?

why: For 'Yes/No' questions in reported speech, we use 'if' or 'whether'. The Simple Present ('revise') shifts to Simple Past ('revised').
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Semira said, "I'm taking my driving test tomorrow."

options.A: She said that I am taking my driving test tomorrow.
options.B: She said that she was taking her driving test the next day.
options.C: She said that she is taking her driving test tomorrow.
options.D: She said that she was taking my driving test the next day.
options.E: She said that I am taking my driving test the following day.

why:
**Rule 1:** Present Continuous ("I'm taking") changes to **Past Continuous** ("she was taking").
**Rule 2:** Pronouns change ("I" to "she", "my" to "her").
**Rule 3:** Time words change ("tomorrow" to "the next day" or "the following day"). Choice B follows all these rules.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

options.A: may
options.B: can
options.C: might
options.D: will

why: This is a reported speech sentence. When the reporting verb is in the past ('said'), the modal 'may' changes to its past form 'might'.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: He complains, “I have a bad headache.”

options.A: He said he has a bad headache.
options.B: He says he has a bad headache.
options.C: He says he had a bad headache.
options.D: He said he had a bad headache.

why: When the reporting verb is in the present tense ('complains'), the tense of the verb in the reported speech does not change. 'I have' becomes 'he has'.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: If it hadn’t been for your help, I couldn’t have done it.

options.A: Had it not been for your help, I could have done it.
options.B: Have not it been for your help, I couldn’t have done it.
options.C: Haven’t it been for your help, I couldn’t have done it.
options.D: Had it not been for your help, I couldn’t have done it.

why: To invert a third conditional sentence, we remove 'if' and move 'had' to the beginning of the clause. The meaning and the rest of the sentence remain the same. 'If it hadn't been' becomes 'Had it not been'.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.
